issues.description: The problem statement uses a snake_case method name `get_total_number_of_students()` (problem_statement.md) while the UML diagram, the template comments, and the solution use the camelCase method name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This naming mismatch in the textual description vs. the UML and code can confuse students about the expected method name/signature.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the problem statement consistent with the UML and code by replacing `get_total_number_of_students()` with the camelCase method name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (and update any textual references). Ensure all places in the description use the same method name/signature to avoid confusion.

issues.description: The problem statement (line 41) refers to the total-students method using snake_case `get_total_number_of_students()`, while the UML, method examples, and the solution implementation use camelCase `getTotalNumberOfStudents()`. This inconsistent identifier for the same conceptual method can create minor mapping confusion for students when they look for the method to implement or call.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent identifier across artifacts. Update the problem statement to refer to the camelCase method name `getTotalNumberOfStudents()` (to match the UML and the solution), or alternatively ensure all references use `get_total_number_of_students()` consistently—preferably adopt camelCase to follow Java naming conventions.
